newsitem.title: CONGO: Brazzaville returns Mobutu's plane to Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Brazzaville returns Mobutu's plane to Kinshasa.

text.p: The presidential Boeing 727 of Zaire's ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko, grounded in Brazzaville in the last days of his rule, was returned to the new Democratic Republic of Congo on Friday, officials said.

The plane arrived in Brazzaville from Mobutu's village of Gbadolite on May 17, the day Laurent Kabila's rebels marched into Kinshasa, to fill up with fuel and fly members of Mobutu's family to safety.
But the crew refused to fly them, saying the plane was state property and now belonged to the new regime. A new crew came on Friday to fly the plane across the Congo river to Kinshasa.

Former Zaire has reverted to the name it held at independence from Belgium in 1960. The Republic of Congo and the Democratic Republic of Congo were founded by competing colonialists France and Belgium in the 1880s.
Congo's President Pascal Lissouba had good relations with Mobutu but Brazzaville is now keen for good relations with the new administration of its giant neighbour.
Mobutu arrived in Morocco from Togo a week ago. A senior Moroccan official said last Saturday that Mobutu was expected to leave for France at the beginning of June.
